_readme: Cross-investor rulings for invariant 10, merged by `verify` at read time (COLLECTION.md §12). `distinct` = the loose name key matched two different companies; `accepted` = the same company, the disagreement is real and explained; `same` = confirmed identity. The shared file data/collection/cross-investor.json is written only at wave alignment, by the designated session, so these live here.

distinct.note: Two different companies behind one word. Felicis's Arena is arena.ai, a private US company the firm's own page says it led the Series A of after seeding. The a16z row cites https://techcrunch.com/2026/01/06/lmarena-lands-1-7b-valuation-four-months -- that is LMArena, which this base holds separately as `lm-arena` and which is now aligned to the same $1.7B figure. Lightspeed's `arena` row cites the same LMArena article and is the same collision.
Same collision as the a16z pair: Lightspeed's row is LMArena, cited to the January-2026 $1.7B round, not arena.ai.

Felicis's Luma is the mesh-WiFi hardware company acquired by First Alert/Newell in 2018. a16z's luma-ai is Luma AI, the video-generation model company that raised $900M in Nov 2025. a16z separately carries its own `luma` row as acquired/below_1b, which agrees with this base exactly -- so the only disagreement is against the wrong company.

Felicis's `guild` is a CMS duplicate of `guild-education` (Denver workforce education) and is merged into it at the rebuild; Redpoint's row is Guild Education itself, held at $4.4B. Once the merge lands the pair compares guild-education to guild-education and the disagreement dissolves. Recorded as distinct only because the surviving slugs differ.

Different companies behind one word. Felicis's Covalent is covalentnetworks.com, a US manufacturing-network company seeded in 2021; Menlo's Covalent Technologies is a separate business it holds as acquired.

Different companies. Felicis's Grove Labs was an indoor-gardening hardware startup that wound down; First Round's Grove is Grove Collaborative, the consumer-products company, which it holds as acquired.
'Aloha' is a bare word and the two rows are on different continents: Felicis's is a 2017 US seed, Cherry's is a European seed it cannot state a status for. No evidence ties them to one company.
Same collision as the Cherry pair; First Round's Aloha is a separate company it holds as defunct.

accepted.note: The same company, and the two runs genuinely disagree: Redpoint bands it 1b_plus citing MotherDuck's own Series B announcement, while a16z holds it below_1b and this run agrees with a16z. Neither side has a figure this run could confirm from a priced event, so the disagreement is recorded rather than papered over, and it is raised for the wave-level alignment where all three bases can be read together.

Same company; this run is the fresher side. Felicis carries the $315M Series E at $5.3B of 2026-02-10 (TechCrunch); a16z and Lightspeed still read below_1b. §10 says the fix is to align the stale side, which is theirs, and a session aligns its own investor rather than editing a sibling's base -- so this is flagged for the wave-level pass.
Same company; this run is the fresher side at $12B (Oct 2025, Nvidia-backed round) against Redpoint's $3B. Flagged for the wave-level pass.
Same company; this run is the fresher side, carrying the $120M Series C at $1.2B of 2026-06-24. Three siblings (First Round, Lightspeed, Menlo) still read below_1b. Flagged for the wave-level pass.
Same company; this run carries the September-2022 $1.55B round (TechCrunch) and Menlo reads below_1b. Flagged for the wave-level pass.

Same company; this run carries the March-2021 $3.2B Series D and a16z reads below_1b. Both marks are stale; the disagreement is about whether the stale primary stands, which §6 says it does absent documented collapse evidence. Flagged for the wave-level pass.

Greylock's published base carries no classification at all -- every column reads None -- so this is a comparison against an unclassified surface rather than a disagreement about a fact. Accepted until Greylock's run lands; nothing on this side needs changing.

Same company. Airware ceased operations in Sept 2018 and its assets went to Delair, which §6 reads as acquired-with-a-successor-note rather than defunct. First Round records defunct; this run applies the §6 convention. Raised for the wave alignment as a convention question, not a fact dispute.
Same company, same §6 convention question: Posterous was acquired by Twitter in March 2012 and shut down afterwards. Acquired-then-shut is `acquired`; Redpoint records defunct.

Possibly the same company and possibly not -- 'Revel' is a bare word, USV's is the mopeds business, and this run's row is a 2020 seed the firm listed without a sector. Accepted pending the wave alignment rather than guessed into a distinct ruling.
